newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan port strike will not affect bunker cargoes.
newsitem.headline: Japan port strike will not affect bunker cargoes.

text.p: Japan's bunker market is unlikely to be affected by a port workers strike scheduled for next week as bunker oil is not handled by the striking unions, traders said on Thursday.
"I just don't see any impact of the strike on the market as bunker oil is not delivered by the unions," one trader with a trading house said.

Workers operating oil barges, which supply bunker oil to vessels, belong to different unions from the National Council of Dock Workers' Unions and the Japan Confederation of Port and Transport Workers' Unions which have decided to stage a 24-hour protest strike on March 12.
They are upset by a U.S. decision to impose sanctions on Japanese ships calling at U.S. ports. The strike would affect operations of container ships docking at all major ports in Japan.

Last week the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission, angry at what it says are costly and discriminatory practices at Japanese ports, said it would slap $100,000 surcharges from April 14 on vessels of Kawasaki Kisen, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK each time they stop at a U.S. port.
